required_floor_classes.lane_definition: A transportation/infrastructure scenario cannot pass if mobility access, service availability, rural/low-density access, disability access, freight access, or household access falls below reviewed floors.
A transportation/infrastructure scenario cannot pass if lower costs are achieved by degrading fatalities, serious injuries, reliability, state of good repair, or project quality.

A transportation/infrastructure scenario cannot pass if service loss, safety risk, fees, construction burden, environmental burden, or access loss shifts to lower-income, rural, disabled, tribal, or underserved communities without review.
A transportation/infrastructure scenario cannot pass if asset condition, maintenance backlog, climate resilience, redundancy, freight continuity, or emergency access falls below reviewed floors.

A transportation/infrastructure scenario cannot pass without an asset inventory, maintenance gap, federal/state/local translation, federal-share costing, delivery schedule, implementation cost, and oversight model.

transportation_infrastructure_specific_f.definition: Bridge, pavement, transit, aviation, water, freight, and other transportation asset condition require sourced floor values before target-cost selection.
Fatalities and serious injuries require sourced baseline, policy, and stress values before any lower-cost scenario can pass.
Passenger reliability, freight reliability, congestion, service continuity, and emergency access require explicit reviewed floors.
Mobility access, rural access, disability access, low-income access, and service availability require explicit thresholds.
Climate resilience, redundancy, mitigation, adaptation, emergency access, and asset-hardening floors require sourced values.
No simulator or target cost can be selected without asset inventory, maintenance gap, federal/state/local translation, federal-share costing, implementation cost, and delivery feasibility.

public_warning_phrases: This transportation/infrastructure floor packet defines required floor concepts, but it does not set threshold values or pass/fail findings.
The transportation pilot floor indicator contract remains thresholdless and does not make the simulator ready.

No lower-cost transportation scenario is admissible until asset condition, fatalities, reliability, access, climate resilience, equity, adequacy/resilience, and delivery-feasibility floors are thresholded, sourced, reviewed, and passed.
No simulator run, target cost, federal effect, gross savings, net savings, solver input, department-cut instruction, technology-savings claim, or balanced-budget claim is populated.
No FOIA request, records request, form, email, phone call, or agency/person contact was submitted.

This record is not outcome-floor passage, not an asset inventory, not a maintenance-gap estimate, not a federal/state/local translation, not a simulator run, not a federal score, not a target-cost selection, not solver input, not a rate calculation, not a public rate card, not a savings estimate, not a waste finding, not a fraud finding, not a department-cut instruction, not a technology-savings claim, and not a balanced-budget claim.
